args: Arguments passed to the external function.
array_parent_dims: Array parent dimensions for expanded array components. When an array component like `plug_p.pin[3]` is expanded to indexed instances (`plug_p.pin[1]`, `plug_p.pin[2]`, `plug_p.pin[3]`), this map stores the parent path `plug_p.pin` with dimensions `[3]` for use in array equation expansion.
array_subscripts: Array subscripts for type alias definitions (e.g., `type Vector3 = Real[3]`) Stores the `[3]` part as subscripts for later use in type resolution
assert_equations: Runtime assertion equations from regular equation sections (MLS §8.3.7). Assertions are preserved for flat output but do not contribute to DAE equation balance/unknown counts.
attribute_source_scopes: Lexical scopes where attribute modifiers were written, keyed by attribute name (`start`, `min`, `max`, `nominal`).
base: The expression to access the field from.
base_def_id: Resolved reference to the base class definition. None when first parsed, populated during name resolution.
base_partitions: Base-clock partitions (execute asynchronously from each other).
binding: The binding expression from `= expr` in declaration (e.g., `Real v = p.v - n.v`) Separate from `start` to preserve binding when both binding and start modifier are present.
binding_from_modification: True if binding came from a modification rather than declaration.
binding_source: Optional symbolic binding source expression for modification-derived bindings. MLS §7.2.4: component modifications are written in an outer scope and may intentionally reference outer parameters (e.g., `gain(g = k)`). We retain this source form for flat-output rendering while keeping `binding` available as a resolved value for semantic passes.
binding_source_scope: Lexical scope where a modification-derived binding was written. Used during flattening to qualify symbolic modifier references according to MLS §7.2.4 without path-depth heuristics.
block_instance: Reference to the block instance for this state.
branches: Branches from Connections.branch(a, b) calls (MLS §9.4). Required edges in the virtual connection graph.
break_names: Component names that are deselected via `break` (MLS §7.4 Selective Model Extension). e.g., extends Base(break x, break y) would have break_names = ["x", "y"]
by_name: Map from type names to TypeIds for quick lookup.
causality: Causality from type alias definition (e.g., `connector RealInput = input Real`) Components of this type inherit this causality
class_def_id: DefId of the class definition this instance was instantiated from.
class_kind: Specialized class kind (model, record, connector, function, etc.).
class_overrides: Active replaceable class/package redeclare overrides for this component instance. Keys are the DefIds of the redeclared local classes (e.g., `Medium`). Values retain the source alias text, effective target DefId, and the redeclare value component reference. Populated during instantiation so downstream phases can apply instance-specific package/class constants consistently (MLS §7.3).
class_type: MLS §4.7: The class type of the root model (model, connector, record, etc.)
class_type_token: Token for the class type keyword (model, class, function, etc.)
classes: Nested class definitions (functions, models, packages, etc.)
clock: The base clock for this partition.
component_ref: Structured component reference that produced this DAE variable, when it corresponds directly to a Modelica component. Generated variables and backend helper slots leave this empty. Compiler logic that needs path structure or resolved identity should use this reference instead of reparsing `name`.
components: Instance data for components, keyed by their InstanceId.
condition: Conditional component expression (e.g., `if use_reset` in `BooleanInput reset if use_reset`) None means the component is unconditional (always present)
conditional: Whether this is a conditional component.
connected: True if this variable is used in connection equations.
connector_type: Reference to the connector type definition.
constants: Constants - fixed values at compile time.
constrainedby: Constraining type for replaceable components (MLS §7.3.2) If set, redeclarations must be subtypes of this type
constructor_exprs: Clock constructor expressions extracted from discrete update equations. These are evaluated against simulation parameters to build tick schedules. This is canonical runtime metadata (always present in DAE schema).
continuous_partition: The continuous-time partition (if any). This contains equations without explicit clock associations.
declaration_source_scope: Lexical scope where this component declaration was written.
def_id: Resolved definition ID (populated by resolve phase). For simple type names, this is the DefId of the class being referenced. For qualified type names (e.g., `Medium.AbsolutePressure`), this may be the DefId of the first part if full resolution fails (partial resolution). Partial resolution indicates the name is valid but depends on a replaceable type parameter that will be resolved during instantiation (MLS §7.3).
def_map: Map from DefId to qualified name (e.g., "Package.SubPackage.Model"). Populated during the resolve phase for O(1) resolved definition lookup.
definite_roots: Connectors with Connections.root() declarations (MLS §9.4.1). These are definite roots for overconstrained connectors, providing implicit equations that don't need to come from external connections. Stores the full path to the overconstrained record (e.g., "pin_p.reference").
description: Optional declaration description string (`"..."` after component declaration).
dims: Array dimensions (None means unknown size, e.g., from `:` subscript).
dims_expr: Unevaluated dimension expressions for parameter-dependent sizes. These are evaluated during flattening when parameter values are known.
disabled_components: Disabled conditional components (MLS §4.8). Contains structured instance component paths whose conditions evaluated to false. These components and their sub-components should be excluded from flattening.
discrete_input_names: Discrete-valued variables whose source causality is input. These are carried in `m` when event/discrete lowering needs them in the runtime discrete partition, but local balance still treats their values as externally supplied inputs.
discrete_reals: Discrete Real variables (z) - change only at events (MLS B.1b).
discrete_valued: Discrete-valued variables (m) - Boolean, Integer, enum (MLS B.1c).
domain: Compact index domain in source binder declaration order.
each: True if the modification has `each` prefix. Note: `each` prefix handling is not yet implemented in the parser.
each_modifications: Set of modification names that have the `each` prefix (MLS §7.2.5). When applied to array components, `each`-prefixed modifications apply the same value to every element, while non-`each` modifications distribute array values.
edges: Edges included in the spanning tree.
elements: Public named elements with their interfaces (recursive).
else_branch: Equations for the else branch (may be empty).
end_name_token: Token for the class name in "end ClassName;" (for rename support)
enum_literal_ordinals: Enumeration literal ordinal map (MLS §4.9.5, 1-based ordinals). Keys are canonical literal paths (e.g. `Modelica.Electrical.Digital.Interfaces.Logic.'1'`), values are integer ordinals used by runtime numeric evaluation.
enum_literals: Enumeration literals for enum types (e.g., `type MyEnum = enumeration(A "desc", B, C)`)
equation_counts: Scalar-view equation count for each domain point in deterministic order.
equation_inactive_rhs: Inactive-guard value for each equation in `equations`.
equations: Continuous implicit equations: 0 = f_x(v, c) (MLS B.1a). All continuous equations in one unified set — no ODE/algebraic/output split.
evaluate: True if this parameter has annotation(Evaluate=true) or is declared final. Structural parameters can be evaluated at compile time for if-equation branch selection (MLS §18.3).
event_actions: Runtime actions evaluated at event instants. `assert` and `terminate` are integration-flow constructs, not numeric residual expressions. `reinit` is lowered earlier into guarded discrete state-update equations and must not appear here.
expandable: True if the class is declared with the `expandable` keyword (MLS §9.1.3) Only meaningful for connector classes
external: External function declaration (MLS §12.9). Only meaningful for function classes.
external_object_name: If derived from ExternalObject, the full name.
final_: True if the modification has `final` prefix. Note: `final` prefix handling is not yet implemented in the parser.
final_attributes: Set of attribute names that are marked as final (e.g., "start" if `final start = 1.0`) When a derived class tries to override these attributes, an error should be raised
first_equation_index: First equation index in the corresponding flat equation vector.
from_expandable_connector: True if this variable comes from an expandable connector (MLS §9.1.3). Unconnected expandable connector members without bindings are unused and shouldn't count as unknowns in the DAE balance calculation.
function_def: The function that computes the residual. Prototype: `function equalityConstraint(a: T, b: T) -> Real[n]`
function_name: External function name (defaults to Modelica function name if not specified).
functions: User-defined functions used by this model (MLS §12).
global_scope: True if import uses global scope (leading dot: `import .A.B.{C, D};`)
has_explicit_binding: True if an explicit binding equation (= value) was provided in the declaration This distinguishes `constant Real c = 0;` (has_explicit_binding=true) from `constant Real c;` (has_explicit_binding=false, even though start may have a default)
has_forwarding_class_redeclare: True when this component applies a self-forwarding class/package redeclare (e.g., `redeclare package Medium = Medium`) that is remapped to an active enclosing override during instantiation (MLS §7.3).
id: Unique identifier within the base partition.
immediate: Whether the transition is immediate (fires at the same instant condition becomes true). Default: true
in_final_state: Whether the state machine is in a final state. MLS §17.2: "stateMachineInFinalState" - no outgoing transitions can fire.
in_spanning_tree: Whether this edge is in the spanning tree.
initial_algorithms: Initial algorithm sections from this instance.
initial_assert_equations: Runtime assertion equations from initial equation sections (MLS §8.6, §8.3.7).
initial_state: The initial state (exactly one state must be marked initial).
initial_structured_equations: Structured source equation families for initial equations.
inner: True if declared with 'inner' prefix (provides instance to outer references)
inner_outer_to_parent_inner: Mapping from inner-outer component paths to their parent inner paths (MLS §5.4). When a component is declared `inner outer` (e.g., `inner outer StateGraphRoot stateGraphRoot`), it bridges two scopes: it serves as `inner` for children and as `outer` referencing the parent. Same-level connections involving the `inner outer` component should redirect to the parent's inner for flow equation scoping (e.g., `makeProduct.stateGraphRoot` → `stateGraphRoot`).
inputs: Input variables (u) - known externally provided values.
instance_id: Unique identifier for this class instance.
interface_flow_count: Count of interface flow variables (MLS §4.7). Per MLS §4.7, flow variables in top-level public connectors count toward the local equation size, not as unknowns. This is because they will receive their defining equations from external connections when the component is used. Interface connectors are identified by containing flow variables but not contributing any behavioral equations (only connectors, not model components).
interiors_materialized: Whether the interior cells' scalar bodies are materialized in the equation vector. `true` (the default) is the historical behavior: every cell carries a full body. When a regular family is lowered with `FlattenOptions::materialize_structured_families = false`, only the corner cells (base + one neighbor per binder) carry real bodies and this is `false`, signaling downstream phases to reconstruct interior incidence/strides from the corners instead of reading the (placeholder) interior bodies.
intervals: Per-variable effective clock interval (seconds) for clocked variables. Keys use canonical flattened variable names (e.g. `pulse.simTime`). This enables spec-compliant evaluation of `interval(v)` where `v` is a clocked variable and the source clock is implicit.
is_class: Whether this represents a class (vs component).
is_connector_type: True if this component's type is a `connector` class (MLS §4.7). Per MLS §4.7, only flow variables in top-level public connector components count toward the local equation size. Models/blocks (like Delta) are NOT interface connectors even if they contain sub-connectors.
is_discrete_type: True if this variable's base type is Integer or Boolean (MLS §4.5). Such variables are discrete by default even without explicit `discrete` prefix. This is used during variable classification to correctly identify discrete variables for the DAE balance calculation.
is_discretized: Whether this is a discretized partition (contains der(), delay(), etc.). MLS §16.8.1: "If the partition contains a Discretized Variables, it is called discretized."
is_final: True if declared with 'final' prefix (cannot be redeclared in derived classes) MLS §7.2.6: "A final declaration in an element modification prevents modification"
is_flow: Whether all variables in this set have flow prefix.
is_initial: Whether this is the initial state (from initialState()). MLS §17.1: "One and only one instance in each state machine must be marked as initial."
is_inside: Whether this is an inside connector (sign = +1) or outside connector (sign = -1). MLS §9.2: "The sign is +1 for inside connectors and -1 for outside connectors."
is_matrix: True if original syntax was `[a;b]` matrix notation, false for `{a,b}` array notation
is_overconstrained: True if this variable belongs to an overconstrained connector (MLS §9.4). A connector is overconstrained if its type defines an `equalityConstraint` function.
is_partial: True if the root model is declared with the `partial` keyword. MLS §4.7: Partial models are incomplete and shouldn't be balance-checked.
is_primitive: True if this variable is a primitive type (Real, Integer, Boolean, String). Record-typed variables (like Complex with .re and .im fields) are not primitive. Non-primitive variables should not be counted as unknowns since their fields are counted separately. MLS §4.8: Balance checking uses expanded scalar counts.
is_protected: True if this component is declared in a protected section (MLS §4.7). Protected components are not part of the public interface and their flow variables should not count as interface flows for balance checking.
is_redeclare: True if declared with element-level `redeclare` prefix.
is_replaceable: True if declared with 'replaceable' prefix (can be redeclared in derived classes) MLS §7.3: "A replaceable element is an element that can be replaced by a different element"
is_stream: Whether all variables in this set have stream prefix.
is_structural: True if this is a structural parameter (MLS §18.3) Structural parameters affect array sizes, for-loop ranges, or if-equation conditions and must be evaluable at translation time.
is_tunable: True if this parameter is tunable at runtime (FMI 3.0 ConfigurationMode). Structural parameters (evaluate=true, Integer/Boolean used for sizing) remain fixed; all other parameters are tunable.
lhs: Left-hand side reference (variable being defined, if any). Explicit equations preserve the structured component reference that produced the lhs. Semantic phases must use this instead of recovering path structure from the rendered variable name.
local: Whether this reference starts with a `.` (local lookup).
location: Full source location spanning from class keyword to end statement
max_span: Source span for the maximum value attribute expression.
min_span: Source span for the minimum value attribute expression.
model_description: Optional description string from the root class declaration.
modifications: Component modifications (e.g., R=10 in `Resistor R1(R=10)`) Maps parameter name to its modified value expression
name: The parameter name token (with source location)
name_map: Inverse map from qualified name to DefId for O(1) resolved definition lookup. This includes non-class definitions such as components. Populated during the resolve phase alongside def_map.
name_token: The token for the component name with exact source location
names: All names imported from the package.
nested_machine: Nested state machine (for hierarchical state machines).
nodes: Nodes in the graph (overdetermined type/record instances).
nominal_span: Source span for the nominal value attribute expression.
num_constraints: Number of scalar constraint equations (n in `Real[n]`).
oc_break_edge_scalar_count: Scalar count of excess equations from VCG break edges (MLS §9.4). Break edges in the overconstrained connection graph generate equality equations that should be replaced by `equalityConstraint()` calls. Until that's implemented, this correction tracks how many excess equation scalars exist.
oc_eq_constraint_size: The output size of the enclosing record's equalityConstraint function. E.g., 3 for Orientation (returns `Real[3]`).
oc_record_path: The path of the enclosing overconstrained record (MLS §9.4). E.g., "frame_a.R" for variables frame_a.R.T and frame_a.R.w. Used to group OC variables into VCG nodes for balance correction.
operator_record: True if the class is declared with the `operator` keyword (MLS §14) Only meaningful for record classes (operator record)
operator_record_base: If this is an operator record, the base class identity.
optional_edges: Optional edges derived from connect() statements for overconstrained nodes (MLS §9.4). These are used together with `branches` when building the virtual connection graph.
origin: Whether this variable corresponds to a source Modelica component or a compiler-generated Appendix B/backend slot.
outer: True if declared with 'outer' prefix (references an inner instance from enclosing scope)
outer_prefix_to_inner: Mapping from outer-prefixed paths to their corresponding inner paths (MLS §5.4). When an outer component `initialStep.stateGraphRoot` references inner `stateGraphRoot`, equations/connections using the outer prefix are redirected to the inner path.
output: Output variable that receives the return value (if any).
outputs: Output variables (left-hand sides of assignments). Used for balance checking per SPEC_0020.
overconstrained_interface_count: Overconstrained interface balance correction (MLS §4.8, §9.4). For overconstrained connector types (e.g., QuasiStatic Reference), this is: N_vars - N_linking_equations - N_explicit_roots where N_vars is the number of overconstrained unknowns, N_linking_equations is the number of equations already linking them (connection equalities + component equations), and N_explicit_roots is the number of explicit root equations (from Connections.root/isRoot). This can be negative when the connection graph has cycles (redundant equations), which is common in polyphase models with adapter components.
parameters: Parameters (p) - fixed values during simulation. MLS Appendix B groups parameters/constants under p; constants remain separately tracked in `constants` for compiler/runtime behavior.
partial: True if the class is declared with the `partial` keyword
parts: The parts of the reference (e.g., `a.b.c` has 3 parts).
potential_roots: Potential roots from Connections.potentialRoot(a, priority) calls (MLS §9.4).
priority: Priority of this transition (MLS §17.1: "priority >= 1"). Lower number = higher priority. Default: 1
pure: True if the function is pure (no side effects). MLS §12.3. Only meaningful for function classes. Functions are pure by default. Set to false when declared with `impure` keyword.
purity_declared: True when the source declared `pure` or `impure` explicitly (MLS §12.3; external functions without an explicit declaration are deprecated, FUNC-032).
qualified_name: Qualified name of the state machine instance.
real_updates: Discrete Real update equations: z = f_z(v, c) (MLS B.1b). Extracted from when-clauses that assign to Real variables.
redeclare: True if the modification is a redeclaration (MLS §7.3).
regular: Family-native classification: present when this family is a regular elementwise stencil whose array accesses are all affine in the binders, carrying the per-access stride table the Solve-IR lowering needs to build a compact `AffineStencil` without materializing one row per index tuple. `None` means the family is materialized the historical (scalar) way.
removed_edges: Edges removed from the spanning tree (will use equalityConstraint).
required: Whether this was a required edge (from Connections.branch()).
required_edges: Edges from Connections.branch() (required - cannot be removed).
reset: Whether the target state is reset when the transition fires. Default: true
resolved_imports: Resolved import map: short name → fully-qualified name (MLS §13.2). Collected from the class definition and its entire inheritance chain. Used during flattening to resolve imported short names (e.g., `pi` → `Modelica.Constants.pi`) instead of incorrectly qualifying them with the component instance prefix.
root_description: Optional description string from the root class declaration.
roots: Root nodes selected for this tree.
scalar_count: Number of scalar equations this represents (MLS §8.4). For array equations like `x[n] = expr`, this is n. For scalar equations, this is 1. Used for balance checking per MLS §4.7.
scheduled_root_conditions: Root rows that correspond to periodic sample schedules. `root_index` is in Solve root-condition order: `conditions.relations`, followed by `events.synthetic_root_conditions`, followed by triggered clock conditions. The schedule fields identify which periodic tick may activate the root at runtime.
scheduled_time_events: Scheduled discontinuity instants derived at compile time. This is canonical runtime metadata (always present in DAE schema).
schedules: Lowered periodic clock schedules. This is canonical runtime metadata (always present in DAE schema).
scope: Scope where the connect statement was declared (flattened prefix). Used to determine the correct hierarchy level for flow sum equations. Empty string means root level.
scope_id: Scope created by this class for name lookup. None when first parsed, populated during name resolution.
scope_to_class: Each class scope's declaring class. Populated during resolve so later phases walk enclosing classes through the scope tree instead of re-parsing qualified names.
sets: All connection sets, indexed by a representative variable name.
shape: Array dimensions - empty for scalars, e.g., [2, 3] for a 2x3 matrix Only populated when dimensions are known literal integers
shape_expr: Raw array dimension subscripts (e.g., `n` in `Real x[n]` or `:` in `Real a[:]`) Used for parameter-dependent dimensions that need runtime evaluation Can be Subscript::Expression for explicit dimensions or Subscript::Range for `:`
shape_is_modification: True if shape is from a modification (shape=x), false if from subscript \[x\]
shift_counter: Shift amount (shiftSample). Number of base clock ticks to shift.
source: Optional source expression before eager resolution. When present, this preserves the symbolic modifier form (`k = parentK`) so downstream flat-output generation can keep parameter propagation relationships instead of hard-coding evaluated defaults.
source_location: Source location of the component declaration that created this instance.
source_map: Source map for mapping file names to SourceIds. Populated during session build for multi-file diagnostics.
source_modification_each_flags: Parallel to `source_modifications` - true if the source modifier has an `each` prefix.
source_modification_final_flags: Parallel to `source_modifications` - true if the source modifier has a `final` prefix.
source_modification_redeclare_flags: Parallel to `source_modifications` - true if the source modifier is a redeclaration.
source_modifications: Ordered source-form modifier arguments from the component declaration. These preserve the syntax inside `x(...)` before semantic component attributes are split into `start`, `binding`, `shape`, and `modifications`.
source_scope: Optional lexical scope where the modifier expression was written. MLS §7.2.4: component modifications are evaluated in the scope where the modification appears, which may differ from the modified component's scope.
source_scope_id: Resolved lexical scope of the class declaration that produced this instance.
source_span: Source span for the `connect`, `Connections.branch`, or related graph-edge source.
span: Source span for error reporting. Never loses source location.
start_has_each: True if the start modifier has `each` prefix (for array components)
start_is_modification: True if start value is from a modification (start=x), false if from binding (= x)
start_span: Source span for the start attribute expression.
statements: The statements in this algorithm section.
states: State variables (x) - continuous variables with derivatives.
structured_equations: Structured source equation families whose scalar views are present in `initial_equations`.
sub_factor: Sub-sampling factor (subSample). The sub-clock ticks every `sub_factor` ticks of the base clock.
sub_partitions: Sub-clock partitions within this base partition.
super_factor: Super-sampling factor (superSample). The sub-clock ticks `super_factor` times per base clock tick.
symbol_ancestry: DefId ancestry for resolved source symbols, ordered from outermost owner to the symbol itself. Used by downstream phases for child/descendant checks without rendered-name prefix matching.
synchronize: Whether to synchronize with sub-state machines of the target state. Default: false
synthesized_inners: Names of inner declarations synthesized during instantiation retry (MLS §5.4). Populated when `outer` components had no matching `inner` and automatic synthesis succeeded.
synthetic_root_conditions: Extra root conditions synthesized from equation expressions beyond canonical `relation`. This is canonical runtime metadata (always present in DAE schema).
template: The family's canonical comprehension body, captured by flatten before the loop is expanded. When present, downstream phases read the template directly (printing it as a `for`-comprehension, deriving strides, building a compact kernel) instead of reconstructing it from materialized corner cells. `None` for families flattened before this representation existed. See [`rumoca_core::ComprehensionTemplate`].
timings: Per-variable effective periodic clock timing for clocked variables. Keys use canonical flattened variable names. This is the phase-bearing companion to `intervals`: `interval(v)` only needs the period, but value-form sample-rate conversion must preserve the variable clock phase when deriving the converted target tick.
top_level_connectors: Names of top-level components whose class type is `connector` (MLS §4.7). Per MLS §4.7, only flow variables in top-level public connector components count toward the local equation size for balance checking. Components of type `model` or `block` (like Delta in transformers) are NOT interface connectors even if they contain connectors internally.
top_level_input_components: Names of top-level components declared with `input` causality. Fields of these components (e.g., `state.phase` from `input Record state`) are external inputs and should NOT be promoted to algebraic unknowns, unlike sub-component inputs from type interfaces (MLS §4.4.2.2).
triggered_conditions: Triggered clock conditions — boolean expressions from non-static Clock() constructors that cannot be resolved to periodic schedules at compile time. These conditions must be evaluated at runtime to determine clock ticks.
type_def_id: DefId of the component's type class (e.g., for `RealInput u`, this is the DefId of RealInput). None for built-in types (Real, Integer, Boolean, String). Populated during name resolution, used by instantiate phase for O(1) type lookup.
type_id: Type of this component, resolved during type checking. None when first parsed, populated during type checking.
type_name: Declared type name from the component declaration. Used by post-instantiation type resolution to recover user-defined type IDs.
type_roots: Canonical type roots for compatibility checks (alias/enumeration normalization). Keys are resolved type identities and values are canonical root type identities. Populated by typecheck_instanced for flatten-time type compatibility.
type_table: All types in the compilation unit.
value: The expression value of the modification. This is the resolved/evaluated form used for semantic checks during instantiation (e.g., conditional component activation).
valued_updates: Discrete-valued update equations: m := f_m(v, c) (MLS B.1c). Extracted from when-clauses that assign to Boolean/Integer/enum variables.
variable: The continuous-time state variable to reinitialize.
variable_final_flags: Flat-output `final` qualifier flags keyed by variable name (MLS §7.2.6). When present and true, codegen should emit `final` before the declaration prefix.
variable_starts: Start expressions for source variables, including variables that may be eliminated from runtime partitions by aliasing. Runtime lowering uses this as semantic metadata for operations such as synchronous back-sampling, where the value before the first source-clock tick is the source variable's `start` attribute.
variable_to_partition: Map from variable name to its associated clock partition.
variable_type_names: Declared flat-output type name for each variable (e.g., Boolean, Integer, MyEnum). Keys match `variables` and values preserve resolved type identity for rendering.
variables: All variables with globally unique names.
